A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original arithmetic-validation experiments, circuit discovery, attention-head interventions, linear probing, and residual-stream patching across four models.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds reverse-patching experiments, other arithmetic operations, and behavioral evaluations of larger models.

M1.justification: Token-wise EAP, soft-intersection circuits, linear probes, consistency-head patching, and the higher-to-lower residual-stream intervention remain unchanged. The added reverse-patching and transfer experiments reuse this machinery without introducing a new model or method component.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates addition word problems. v2 adds subtraction, multiplication, and division, with eight templates per operation and two-digit/one-digit operand settings described in Appendix C.1 and Table 10. These tasks are actually evaluated in Table 7 and the intervention experiments in Figures 9 and 19.

E2.justification: The unmodified-model and random-head-patching controls remain, with identical comparison-head lists in v1 Table 3 and v2 Table 4. The larger models are additional study configurations; no new competing circuit-discovery or correction method is evaluated.

E3.justification: v2 substantially expands the tested model scales by adding Qwen-2.5-32B-Instruct and Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct. It also adds reverse patching with alpha = 1.0 over 1,000 prompt pairs, while retaining the original forward-patching factors of 3.1-3.4 (Appendix D.4). New operation evaluations use 1,000 pairs per template; existing circuit-discovery and probe-training settings are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's interventions that restore error detection, v2 tests whether reversing the activation transfer suppresses detection (Figures 6 and 18). It also tests whether the same addition-identified heads influence validation for other operations (Figures 9 and 19). These substantially extend the causal diagnostics and generalization analyses.

E5.justification: v2's Figure 3 caption explicitly identifies the existing error bars as standard deviations across templates; v1 describes only average faithfulness. Otherwise, reporting continues to use means and standard deviations across templates. No new seed information, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, or significance-testing procedure is introduced.

E6.justification: v2 adds reverse-patching outcomes and operation-specific and larger-model results. Table 8 reports Llama-3.1-70B accuracy of 100% for either single-position error but 44.76% for consistent errors; Table 7 reveals exceptions to the failure pattern, including Phi-3. Figure 6 also revises existing forward-patching bars, with patched Qwen accuracy approximately 0.90 in v1 and 0.84 in v2, without explaining the revision. Original accuracy and circuit tables retain their values.

T1.justification: The soft-intersection definition, EAP approximation, faithfulness formula, and circuit-overlap definitions are unchanged. Appendix D.4 generalizes source/target notation for the existing patching operation, without adding a theoretical result, assumption, proof, or substantive derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract narrows the proposed explanation from failures of 'current LLMs' to 'smaller-sized LLMs,' and the introduction makes the basic math-word-problem scope clearer. The central claims about consistency heads, structural dissociation, and residual-stream interventions remain; the conclusion is unchanged.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 newly explains incomplete reverse-patching effects through potentially unpatched consistency heads and circuit incompleteness. Sections 4.4 and 7 tentatively extend the consistency-head explanation to larger models, while acknowledging Phi-3's different behavior on other operations. These qualify and extend the retained mechanistic interpretation.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 and Table 10 provide templates, verb choices, and operand restrictions for the added operations. Appendix D.4 documents the reverse intervention and its scaling factor. Code access, original head lists, probe hyperparameters, software, precision, and hardware-budget disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Meng et al. (2022) for activation patching and Mondorf et al. (2025) for circuit completeness, and removes the Chern et al. (2024) Factool reference. The principal positioning relative to self-correction and mechanistic arithmetic research remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Local rewrites clarify token positions, layer ranges, intervention directions, and task scope. v2 adds Section 4.4, expands Appendix D.4, and updates affiliations and acknowledgments. The overall section sequence and most existing prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 6 and the appendix head-patching plots are redrawn to display both intervention directions. v2 adds Figures 9 and 19 and Tables 7, 8, and 10, and moves v1's appendix Table 6 into the main text as Table 2. Captions and figure placement change locally; the overall layout and existing circuit and attention visualizations are retained.

improvement.justification: The reverse interventions and transfer tests provide useful new checks on the consistency-head explanation, while larger-model evaluations and narrower framing improve the assessment of its scope. The gains are tempered by reporting weaknesses: Section 4.4 overlooks Qwen-2.5-1.5B's multiplication exception in Table 7, Appendix E.3 gives 44.67% where Table 8 gives 44.76%, and revised forward-patching values are unexplained. Overall, v2 provides better empirical support and qualifications, with a limited net quality improvement.
